page: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The system is configured with 40 shared vCPUs, which correspond to 20 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 768 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 123693.48 and a PassMark CPU score of 72888.75. Memory performance is notable for its top-tier large-block read-only bandwidth of 451.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 262.45 GB/sec. Database performance is supported by a strong Redis SET operations benchmark of 84.31 million operations per second, alongside average-tier performance in standard database operations and static web serving throughput.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff in environments requiring sustained, non-variable compute performance. However, the high density of 40 vCPUs and 160 GB of RAM provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that can tolerate shared resources. This hardware profile is best suited for multi-threaded data processing, database hosting, and general-purpose web serving applications.
